newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: GOV'T SUGGESTS $101 MILLION BUTINGE CREDIT.
newsitem.headline: GOV'T SUGGESTS $101 MILLION BUTINGE CREDIT.

text.p: The Lithuanian government decided on Wednesday to appeal for parliament's approval to issue a state guarantee to six foreign banks for $101.56 million worth of credits for construction of the Butinge oil terminal.
"A draft law on financing construction of the Butinge oil terminal was approved and it will be passed on to parliament for its consideration," the government's press office said.

The draft law proposes issuing state guarantees to the Union Bank of Switzerland (U.S. affiliate) and U.S. EXIM Bank, Kreditanstalt fur Wiederaufbau, Union Bank of Switzerland (Switzerland), Bank of Tokyo Mitsubishi, Nordic Investment Bank and Merrill Lynch International.
It also says that individual contracts and terms of the credit should be negotiated with each bank individually, but the total sum should not exceed $101.56 million.
Butinge said earlier that it needed $202 million in credits.
The government refused to issue state guarantees for more than the $101.56 million since its stake in the company will be reduced to 34 percent from 85.5 percent following Butinge's new share issue.
The current share capital of the company is 71.2 million litas, but the company decided to boost it to 260 million litas.
The subscription for the new share issue is to start on July 2, and is planned to end by August 15.
